Armitage Auctions, Invermay (Launceston). Online auction closing Wednesday 21 October 2026, each lot at its own time (ADST). The catalogue is going up in parts on Friday 16 October.

Armitage 21 October

All four catalogues posted so far (lots 601 to 952, 953 to 1286, 1349 to 1677 and 1681 to 1968) are fully checked. Lots 1 to 600 and 1287 to 1348 had not been posted when this page was built. Every photo of all 1,290 lots was viewed and scoring was blind to the estimate and bids. Best supported: a 9ct gold bangle, 34.8 g (lot 886, keep max $1,330, bid $700 when checked), a Louis Vuitton Initiales reversible belt (746, keep max $530, bid $50), 15ct cufflinks (905, $490), an old joiner's workbench (1937, $340), a 16-drawer workshop drawer bank (1828, $295), 9ct rose gold cufflinks (904, $260), a La-Z-Boy power recliner (1227, $245), three small Pro Hart hand-coloured etchings (764, 766, 785, about $170 to $185 each), a French carriage clock (661, $210), a Keith Naughton oil (1108, $210) and a Geoff Tyson watercolour (1013, $210). Seen at the viewing on 17 Oct: the Tudor Oyster (883) is a ref 7934 of about 1957-58 with an original honeycomb dial and Rolex-signed crown, keep max $620 on the lowest sold comp, and worth more to the right buyer. Look at the viewing: a Dior saddle pouch (818), an 18ct Hunt & Roskell pocket watch (874), S. Kirk & Son sterling (642), a complete Endemic Flora of Tasmania (683), an enclosed Shoprider cabin scooter (1159) and packs of new Tasmanian oak lining. From lots 1349 to 1677: an early brass-bladed electric desk fan (1412, $210), a Cyclops pedal car (1355, $190) and several James Bond diecast collections ($70 to $90 each); look at the 1975 Mercedes 280S (1349), a Honda Legend coupe (1354), a Lister D-type engine (1677) and a Hot Toys quarter-scale Batman (1424).

Run details

Closing
Each lot closes at its own time on Wednesday 21 October; the time is on every card and on the lot page countdown. Bid before the lot's own close.
Viewing
Viewing on Wednesday 21 October from 8:30 AM at 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay. Phone (03) 6326 2555.
Viewing checklist
  • Lot 25 (closes 12:38 pm): check the edition of The Little Black Princess. The first edition is Alexander Moring Ltd (De La More Press), London, 1905, green pictorial cloth; the 1906 'second edition' is a second printing; the common Robertson & Mullens, Melbourne, printings from the 1920s on are worth little. Dealers ask $1,200 for a 1905 first and $600 for a 1906. Also note the printing dates in the six Bean volumes.
  • Lot 39 (12:42 pm): Robbery Under Arms. Confirm all three volumes are Remington and Co, London, 1888, in matching green cloth; look for library stamps, missing half-titles or adverts, and cracked hinges.
  • Lot 883 (5:24 pm): Tudor Oyster 7934. Wind it and watch the seconds hand; check the crown screws down.
  • Lot 874 (5:21 pm): 18ct half hunter. Ask for the weight in grams and to see the valuation; look for the hallmark inside the case backs.
  • Lot 818 (5:02 pm): Dior and Prada pouches. Check the Dior serial tag and the Prada Milano plate and serial label.
  • Lot 683 (4:18 pm): Endemic Flora of Tasmania, Parts I to VI. Check all six parts are present with their plates and the original wrappers or boxes.
  • Lot 365 (2:31 pm): red acrylic bar stools. Look underneath for a moulded Kartell mark.
  • Lot 142 (1:17 pm): Singer 222K. Check the free arm, the motor runs and the case has the controller and accessories.

Assumptions
  • Every lot in each catalogue was taken from Armitage's public group page, and every lot page and every photo was fetched at full size. Nothing was bid, watched, logged in to or submitted.
  • Scoring is blind to price: the Armitage estimate, current bid and bid count were removed from the data the scan, rescore and research agents saw. They are shown on this page for information only.
  • Buyer's premium is 22% including GST on the hammer price, as shown on every lot page. All-in = hammer x 1.22.
  • Candidates with a blind score of 4 or more got a market pass (Tasmanian past results first: Armitage's own and Gowans' public results, then other auction houses, marketplaces and dealers). Every flagged lot was then re-checked by Opus, which re-read the photos and opened every comp, dropping any that did not match.
  • Maximum bids use only sold prices in the last 24 months for the same item in similar condition. Melt value for gold and silver is a floor, not a sale, so it never sets a maximum bid.
  • Gold and silver weights, carat marks and maker claims in the titles are catalogue claims. Check weights and hallmarks at the viewing.
  • Pickup only from 9 Goodman Crt, Invermay. Inbound freight assumed $0 (local).
  • Sources closed to this session (eBay, Wine-Searcher, Australian Whisky Auctions) were not used directly.

FLIP picks (buy to resell)

KEEP picks (buy to own)

Lot 953 closes Wed 21 Oct 5:48 PM

Hand-knotted wool tribal rug, 188 x 118 cm (size from the lot description). It has a dark navy field with three stepped rust and aubergine medallions and stepped guard borders. The design is Baluch (Afghan or East Persian Baluchi), not a classic Turkoman gul rug, although Armitage calls it Afghan Tu

Medium confidence score 5/10

Photo findings
Three studio cut-out photos. Classic Baluch layout: three stepped medallions on a navy field, white accent motifs and several stepped borders. Pile looks even and full and colours are strong, with no visible holes or stains. The fringe is short and even at one end. No label or back photo.
Condition
Appears good from the photos. The back, pile depth, moth and sides are not visible.
Current bid
No bids yet at 16/10/2026 17:49 AEDT
Armitage estimate
300-500 (not used in scoring)
Suggested max
KEEP max hammer $95 (all-in $115.90) (all-in = hammer x 1.22)
Market guide
$120 to $300 All evidence is Gowans Hobart hammer prices in AUD, with buyer's premium extra. Six same-type Baluchi rugs of 170-220 cm length sold at $120-300 hammer between Sep 2025 and Sep 2026, median about $265. One of those rugs passed in twice before selling at $300. Category guides (Afghan Turkman, Ashak and Balouchi of other sizes) run $100-260, and room-size Turkman rugs reach $410-460. No asking prices. Rate 1.0, all AUD.

Working and confidence

Why Low: Identification as cast iron rests on the title only (could be aluminium reproduction), no maker mark, and the SOLD evidence is single panels of different designs, scaled up to four.

Dropped entries: eBay AU 276508525132 (AU$335, 14 lacework pieces) dropped: snippet only, eBay is closed to us so it cannot be opened, and it is frieze/fretwork, not balustrade panels.

Working: No sold set of four found, so values are scaled from single-panel Gowans sales (close, not same). Keep: lowest single SOLD $25 x 4 panels = $100; $100 / 1.22 = $81.97, round down to $80. Flip: likely Tasmanian resale about $50 a panel from the $30-$70 bid-supported singles, so 4 x $50 = $200; less about 20% auction seller fees ($40) and $0 postage (bulky, local pickup sale) = $160; $160 / 2.44 = $65.57, round down to $65. A buyer restoring a verandah would pay well above this (dealer $240 each), which is the upside, not the bid basis.

Ask Armitage: Are these genuine cast iron (heavy, magnet sticks) or aluminium reproductions? Any cracks, broken lugs or welded repairs? Please confirm sizes.
